reports.title: The BLM continues to work on repairs on the Wilson Reservoir Campground Road
reports.text: Bass fishing has still been good with fish over 15″ reported.

reports.title: As of 9/20/26, Wild Horse Reservoir remains under a HAB Watch Advisory
reports.text: Bass fishing remains good, with fish hanging around rocky outcroppings and submerged vegetation. Wacky rig Senkos, flukes under a dropshot, and chatterbaits with trailers are some recommended set ups. As of July 1, anglers can keep 1 black bass and 1 wiper. Minimum size for black bass and wiper is 15 inches total length.

reports.title: Surface water temps are hovering around 64 degrees
reports.text: Bass fishing remains good around the reservoir. Bass are hitting dark colored soft plastics in rocky areas and weed edges. As of July 1, anglers can keep 1 black bass and 1 wiper. Minimum size for black bass and wiper is 15 inches total length.

reports.title: Water temperatures are sitting at 60F
reports.text: Largemouth Bass activity should remain good through the first few weeks of early October; with the bite picking up late morning through the afternoon. Target the south end of the lake for these fish. Expect to catch 11-to-13-inch Largemouth Bass. A variety of lures are being used to catch bass, such as shallow retrieving Rapalas, soft plastics, and some poppers. Northern Pike angling has produced multiple fish in the 5-to-10-pound range. The fall bite for Pike should produce for anglers focusing on the south end of the south lake. reports.title: The best action has occurred south of Big Bend State Park
reports.text: Smallmouth bass are reacting well to creature baits thrown along drop-offs.

reports.title: Anglers continue to catch bluegill, bass and catfish throughout the day
reports.text: Anglers continue to catch bluegill, bass and catfish throughout the day. A few bass have been caught on 3-inch craws and Ned rigs.
